I remember when I first found out about Reddit in 2010. It didn't interest me initially because all I saw was the front page, however a little later my friend began showing me a bunch of small subreddits. I was amazed with how many interesting communities and discussions their were and I've been using Reddit ever since.

I have a few controversial views on the world, like I'm sure most people do, and Reddit was always been the perfect place for me to discuss those views, often with an entire subreddit and community dedicated to just that topic.

I understand why illegal content needs to be removed, but in a world where ideas and politics are being discussed more and more frequently online, extremely open and accepting communities in my opinion are a super important thing to have. I don't support or agree with communities which shame fat people for example, but as long as they do it within the law, I see no reason why I, or anyone else, shouldn't allow those kinds of communities to exist. Especially, when you consider how many people obviously enjoyed what they were doing.

Reddit is a private company, they can do whatever they want. But I personally want to use a platform which I know everything I read will honest and uncensored. I want the people I disagree with on subreddits like FPH to discus with me why I should join them and hate fat people. I want people and communities who will tell me why feminism is good, and others to tell me why feminism is bad. I want to hear from people on the left and right of the political spectrum. I no longer get that on Reddit because of how hard they're pushing their community into conforming to extreme-left social standards. Now when I see a comment thread I question whether what I am read is really the views of the people, or just the views of people who haven't been shadow banned or driven off of the site completely for their opposing views.

So here I am. =) I'm looking forward to finding some awesome subverses.
